milestone: M37 External Mode Pack Active Lifecycle

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds explicit Rust-owned rollback from the active Mode Pack snapshot to the immediately previous rollback-capable snapshot.
mode.list, mode.get, permission.check, and task.start consume the restored snapshot after rollback.
Rollback records bounded current and restored snapshot summaries without raw Mode Pack JSON or raw ledger payloads.
Headless callers can recover active external Mode Pack policy after a bad replacement without manual state edits.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances mode_pack_runtime directly, with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: The Rust runtime can roll back an active Mode Pack replacement to a bounded previous snapshot captured during rollback-capable replacement, using explicit authorization and expected current/rollback fingerprints.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M12.3 activation and M37.1 replacement cannot restore prior active policy without manual state mutation, and M37.1 summary-only evidence lacks compiled policy snapshots.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: External Mode Pack lifecycle can move forward through replacement but cannot recover from a bad active update in headless operation.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M37.1 replaced active state from a live validated candidate; M37.2 captures rollback-safe prior state and restores it from bounded lifecycle evidence.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. Existing read RPCs cannot mutate active state and modepack.replaceActive requires a live candidate rather than rollback evidence.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The result carries bounded current/restored snapshot summaries as execution evidence, not a report/history/digest/readiness wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: modepack.rollbackActive validates authorization and fingerprints, restores the previous bounded snapshot, records bounded rollback evidence, and makes active-mode consumers use the restored snapshot.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can deterministically recover active external Mode Pack policy after a replacement without manual file edits.
answers.milestone_progress: M37 gains the recovery counterpart to replacement, making local active lifecycle closeout viable before later remote acquisition/trust work.

exit_criteria: modepack.rollbackActive requires explicit rollback authorization and an existing active snapshot
The runtime rejects stale current activation fingerprints before writing
The runtime rejects rollback activation fingerprint mismatches before writing
The runtime rejects missing rollback-capable replacement evidence and legacy summary-only replacement evidence before writing
A valid rollback writes one bounded restored active snapshot and records bounded current/restored evidence
Replaying the same rollback returns the same rollback event id and does not append duplicate rollback evidence
mode.list, mode.get, permission.check, and task.start consume the restored snapshot after rollback

Ledger, RPC, store, and VSIX payloads contain no raw Mode Pack JSON, prompt, provider response, file content, stdout/stderr, command, environment, raw ledger payload, absolute path, canonical path, or secret
VSIX validators accept valid rollback results and reject malformed fingerprints or raw payload fields

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M37.2 changes product runtime/protocol/store/VSIX behavior and phase manifests; review must confirm this is active snapshot rollback, not another wrapper surface.
